newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen flat next week before KGHM IPO.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen flat next week before KGHM IPO.

text.p: The Polish bourse is seen flat or easing next week as investors save up for copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA's public offering, which begins on June 30, analysts said.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.6 percent this week to 16,048.1 points
Analysts said Wednesday's news the institutional tranche of Bank Handlowy's privatisation offer was 17.5 times subscribed boded well for KGHM as well as Handlowy, both among Poland's largest firms.

"After the big success of the Bank Handlowy offer, demand for KGHM could be at least as big and...perhaps, investors will refrain from buying on the bourse, leading to a flat trend," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Foreign demand exceeded $3.5 billion for Handlowy, which will start bourse trade on either June 26 or June 30.
Analysts said the state treasury must have sensed the potential demand for KGHM because it raised on Friday KGHM's price range for the offering to 18-23 zlotys from 15-23 zlotys.
Mediocre May earnings results this week also kept investors from buying listed stocks this month, analysts said, noting that the market seemed fairly valued.
"It seems either some prices have to fall or earnings go up more significantly for there to be many stocks to buy," said Piotr Leszczuk, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
But analysts said Poland's solid macroeconomic environment, underlined by news on Friday first-quarter gross domestic product gained 7.3 percent, would prevent a steep fall in stocks.
Poland's cut of 1997's year-on-year inflation target to 12 percent from 13 was also seen as encouraging.
Analysts also said stocks could be buouyed if money from the Handlowy oversubscription flowed to listed stocks as well as to KGHM.
On Friday, the bourse also said National Investment Funds (NFIs) in Poland's mass privatisation programme start continuous trade on July 1.
Analysts said parliament's statement on Friday that it would vote on a capital gains tax exemption for the funds had largely been discounted.
